result.reason: Nothing I found kills the claim. § 49(4) PBefG has allowed electronic and app-based order logs since 2021, and the July 2026 amendment did not change § 49. The BGH upheld the return duty on 3 June 2026 (I ZR 123/25). VGH München 11 CS 26.1088 (7 August 2026) upheld revocation of 8 permits after the authority demanded the order book plus app order data on USB and ran a time-series analysis that found 50 return-duty breaches in 175 trips. I found no vendor selling an order book that checks the return duty. Uber's supplier portal and FREENOW's dashboard capture orders but do not check return compliance. The score stays low because many Uber and Bolt fleet owners avoid the duty on purpose, enforcement depends on the authority and is mostly triggered by suspicion, and reform lobbying continues. The TSE part is already crowded.

result.competitor: No craft-focused multi-country SaaS found. Equus Platform automates posted-worker filing with RPA and APIs for AT, CY, GR, HU, IE, NL, SE and PT; it is aimed at enterprises. NIUMAD is an online service that collects posted-worker data. Done-for-you consultancies (Eurofiscalis, arlettipartners/Studio A&P) act as the French representative and file SIPSI. The IHK and HWK chambers give advice and fill-in guides but do not file. The future free EU eDeclaration portal is the main threat. Not checked in this session: DATEV and other payroll software for A1 filing.
result.duty: Host-country law, not German law. Austria (LSD-BG): a ZKO3 notice to the BMF Zentrale Koordinationsstelle before work starts (up to one week before). For repeat postings under one contract, one notice can cover up to 6 months. Sole traders without employees are exempt. France: a SIPSI prior declaration for each posting, even for one-day services, plus a mandatory representative in France. The IHK sheet gives fines of 4,000 EUR per undeclared worker, up to 500,000 EUR. Belgium: Limosa. An A1 certificate is needed per posting. EU eDeclaration: provisional deal on 2026-06-23, still awaiting formal adoption. It is voluntary for member states, has no go-live date, and the ZDH notes A1 is not yet linked to it. Not checked: the Netherlands, Italy, Spain, Czechia, Luxembourg and Switzerland procedures.
result.market: KPMG, citing EU PD A1 data, puts Germany as the top issuing country in 2024 with about 2.1M PD A1 certificates. Older Bundestag figures show about 230k per year for 2010-2016 (Drucksache 19/2806); the two series are not directly comparable. The number of German craft firms that post workers each year was not found.
result.reason: The duties are real, but they come from each host country's law, not German law. Austria requires a ZKO3 notice under the LSD-BG before work starts (BMF/WKO). France requires a SIPSI declaration plus a named representative, even for one-day jobs, with fines of 4,000 EUR per worker. I found no cheap multi-country tool built for craft firms. Equus automates some countries for enterprise mobility teams, and consultancies such as Eurofiscalis and arlettipartners sell the service. The trilogue deal of 2026-06-23 creates a single EU eDeclaration portal that the Commission will build. It is optional for states, has no start date, and once a state joins it replaces that state's portal. That threatens the core value of form-filling. Postings are frequent, about 2.1M PD A1s issued in DE in 2024, but the market's lifespan is uncertain.

result.competitor: The TSE part is crowded: taximeter and Wegstreckenzähler hardware vendors, fiskaly cloud TSE through FMS (per the claim), and Hale. It should be left out of scope. For the order book, the FREENOW AGB require Mietwagen firms to record and forward orders through FREENOW's Fleet Partner Dashboard, so platforms already partly capture order intake. Uber's supplier portal manages the fleet, drivers and revenue. I found no evidence that it produces a § 49 order book. FahrerApp (meinfahrer.app) is Mietwagen-specific telematics with shift recording and seat-occupancy sensors. Its listing does not mention the order book, return-duty proof or TSE. SuE-TaMi Dispo, SOLU Driver and Taxi.de are dispatch tools. Fleetster, Vimcar and R-DRIVE are general electronic logbooks. I found no product that merges platform orders, GPS returns and follow-on order IDs into a register the licensing authority can audit and that flags return-duty breaches. The VG Ansbach case shows authorities now ask for exactly that data.
result.duty: The duty is real, federal and in force. Under § 49 Abs. 4 PBefG, a Mietwagen may only carry out orders that arrive at the firm's base. The firm must record each incoming order in a book or electronically and keep the record for 1 year. After each trip the car must return to the base straight away unless it already has a follow-on order. The current text on gesetze-im-internet.de still contains the return duty. On 2026-06-03 the BGH (I ZR 123/25) upheld the return duty as constitutional and held that breaching it is unfair competition. Enforcement is active. In VG Ansbach AN 10 S 26.536 (16.07.2026), the authority demanded the order register on USB plus machine-readable platform trip data with return times and follow-on order IDs. It counted 67 breaches in 210 trips and revoked permits for 16 cars without a prior warning, and the court upheld this. VGH München 11 ZB 20.2076 upheld a sanction for a badly kept order book. Separately, under § 146a AO, KassenSichV and the BMF letter of 11.03.2024, taximeters and Wegstreckenzähler need a TSE from 2026-01-01. Breaches can be fined up to EUR 25,000 (Härting). The device must also be reported to the Finanzamt via ELSTER within 1 month. One summary says older Wegstreckenzähler with a digital interface may be connected to a TSE until 31.12.2026. Härting and the Berlin LABO page give 1.1.2026 as the hard date. I could not resolve this because the MV Merkblatt PDF was unreadable.
result.market: I found no current national count. The DTMV figure via Statista is just over 53,000 taxis in Germany in 2016. The federal survey every four years (last cited for 31.12.2016) and Brandenburg's answer (data held only by districts) give no Mietwagen firm count. Mietwagen permits have no cap, and the Uber/Bolt-driven fleet segment is large in big cities. I estimate roughly 20,000 to 30,000 taxi and Mietwagen firms in total, mostly with 1 to 5 vehicles. This is unverified.
result.reason: The pain is real and rising. The BGH upheld the return duty in June 2026, and VG Ansbach shows permits revoked for a missing or incomplete machine-readable order register. Owner-operators face daily record-keeping. The weak points: the TSE part is solved by hardware vendors. Platforms (FREENOW dashboard, Uber portal) already hold most order data, so a tool would be an aggregation and audit layer. Some heavy Mietwagen users break the return duty on purpose and won't buy proof tools. Political proposals to abolish the return duty add regulatory risk. Buyers are fragmented, price-sensitive and reached through taxi associations or IHK. An MVP needs platform data imports and GPS, so it is not trivial. It is a niche gap worth testing but carries risk.

result.competitor:
I found no dedicated tool that classifies KSA-liable payments. Partial substitutes cover most of the job:
- The free federal online form on verwaltung.bund.de takes about 5 minutes and uses an ELSTER certificate or eID, so the claim's card-reader barrier looks outdated.
- The paper form the KSK mails out each year.
- Ausgleichsvereinigungen under § 32 KSVG handle the duty for about 71k Verwerter.
- Accounting software: Lexware has KSA guidance and dedicated accounts (Haufe gives 4391/6431 for SKR03/04), and a provider claims lexoffice automates KSK bookings.
- Tax advisers.
- Free online calculators such as steuerschroeder.de.
result.duty: KSVG (federal). Companies liable for the levy must report the previous year's net fees paid to self-employed artists and publicists to the KSK by 31 March without being asked. Typical exploiters (publishers, agencies, galleries) must file a zero report if they paid nothing. The levy is 4.9% in 2026 (ordinance published September 2025) and 5.0% in 2027, with monthly advance payments. For companies that use artists only occasionally, the de minimis limit rose to 1,000 EUR in 2026; typical exploiters are always liable. The DRV must reach every employer every four years by audit or consultation. It audits about 40% of employers with up to 19 staff, covering 4 to 5 calendar years, and late or wrong reports lead to an estimate. I did not check the amount of fines in this session.
result.market: A Bundestag answer gives about 157k companies paying the levy in 2019 and about 156k in 2020 (preliminary). About 71k more meet the duty through Ausgleichsvereinigungen. The DRV audits about 400k employers a year, so far more small firms are potentially liable but not registered. I found no figure newer than 2020.
result.reason: The duty is real federal law (KSVG). Companies that use self-employed artists or publicists file a report by 31 March, including a zero report if they paid nothing. The levy is 4.9% in 2026 and returns to 5.0% in 2027, and it is paid in monthly advances. The DRV covers every employer at least every four years. It audits about 40% of employers with up to 19 staff and covers 4 to 5 past years, and the KSK or DRV estimates the levy if no report is filed. No dedicated KSA product turned up. However, the filing itself is a 5-minute online form on the federal portal (verwaltung.bund.de) with an ELSTER certificate, so the card reader in the claim is outdated. About 71k firms already file through Ausgleichsvereinigungen, and tax advisers or accounting tools handle the rest. That leaves only the job of sorting which payments count, done once a year, so willingness to pay is low.

Duty is real: Entlastungsbetrag (§45b SGB XI, 131 EUR/month) is refundable only for Land-recognised or registered Angebote. Helpers must issue monthly Leistungsnachweise, and Bayern requires an annual Tätigkeitsbericht. Three searches found no software for solo helpers, only Land PDF forms and consumer guides. But this is not a mandatory recurring duty to an authority. It is optional billing, and the helpers are tiny earners. Rules differ across 16 Länder, and 8 EUR/hour caps limit willingness to pay. Pflegesoftware for ambulante Dienste was not checked. No national count of recognised helpers was found. Weak buyer, fragmented rules, and a 1-page form is a close substitute.

Duty is real: §23(2) SGB VIII gives half-refund of pension and health/care contributions on application, accident insurance refunded in full. Deadlines differ by Jugendamt (Esslingen: by 15 Jan of the following year). It is an annual form task, not a heavy compliance duty. No software found aimed at self-employed Tagespflegepersonen. Existing tools are Kita or municipal systems (KAI, Kita-Abrechnung, KiPro, ITEBO NH-Tagespflege), which are not sold to individuals. Market is about 40,000 persons, shrinking about 11% from 2020 to 2024. Pain is low, willingness to pay is weak, forms are Jugendamt-specific and fragmented, and the duty is mostly form-filling, so the MVP is thin. Competition is absent but demand is small. The 40,000 figure is an inference from a Prognos-derived "knapp 45.000 bis 2020" less 11%, not a 2025 Destatis count.

Duty is real: AwSV (federal) requires expert checks for underground tanks and larger above-ground Heizöl tanks (over 10,000 l, or from 1,000 l in protection zones) every 5 years, or 2.5 years in water-protection areas. Transition rules in §70 AwSV give first-check deadlines up to Aug 2027. No operator-side deadline-tracking software found in 3 searches; TÜV offers reminders and authority notification as part of its inspection service. Market is large in theory (about 5.4M tank systems per an older IWO table, my own sum), but most are private households, not businesses. Prüfpflichtige share is unknown. Low willingness to pay, intervals every 5 years, inspectors already own the customer relationship, and rules differ by Land. Weak SaaS fit. Related to K04.

Section 38 GewO only lets the Länder issue such ordinances. The NRW and Bavaria texts found are dated 1985, and I could not confirm they are in force. The IMK recommendation of Dec 2012 is known only from a Sachsen-Anhalt Landtag inquiry. Sachsen-Anhalt declined to introduce a duty (2013). The Brandenburg administrative rule lapsed in 1998. I found no current Land list and no penalty or frequency figures. The Sachsen-Anhalt PDF was unreadable. The one Land ordinance seen is a plain numbered book (a paper book or spreadsheet suffices), so buyers have little reason to pay for software. The buyer count is unknown. Two searches found no dedicated software. This is a small, fragmented, possibly lapsed niche. K32 was rejected for the same reason.

The duty is real: Austria requires a ZKO3 online notification before work starts, plus a contact person (§23 LSD-BG). France requires SIPSI notification and a named representative. The A1 certificate must be carried, and fines are per worker and can be high. The market is large: Austria logged about 23,000 German-sender notifications in 2016, about 5,100 of them construction, and Germany issues about 220,000 A1s a year (older data). No craft-specific multi-country tool turned up in my searches, only consultancies. Weaknesses: the EU eDeclaration (trilogue deal 23 June 2026, a 41-field form) may remove much of the pain; the portals are free; firms post irregularly; the ZDH wants the A1 linked in. I did not check DATEV or HWK services, Switzerland, or product names. Score is 4.

The duty is real. EU Reg 2016/2031 requires registration and authorisation, passports on trade units, and records kept 3 years. The Länder plant protection services run it, for example LK Schleswig-Holstein and RP Giessen. Two caveats: the traceability code is usually not required for finished goods, and the duty is mostly label printing plus records. Competition could not be settled. Searches found no dedicated plant-passport software, but nursery and horticulture ERP and label printers such as Koenig & Bauer probably cover passport labels. The KTBL software guide was blocked (Access Denied). No national count of authorised operators was found. The only figure is old Sachsen data from 2013 (50 Baumschulen, 83 Jungpflanzen producers). The market is probably a few thousand firms, many already served by ERP vendors. That makes the niche small, with weak willingness to pay.

Duty is real: EU Reg 2024/1028 applies since 2026-05-20. The BNetzA data hub has run since 2026-07-01. Where a municipality has a registration procedure, hosts need one number per unit and must show it in every listing. Platform fines run up to 100,000 EUR, and the duty falls on the platforms, not hosts. Registration is opt-in by Land and municipality, and BNetzA says no new procedures are planned. Only a few places are named (e.g. München, Nürnberg, Regensburg, Tübingen from 2026-10-01), and Thüringen has none. The host-side job is one-off: apply once, enter the number once. Hosts are hobby-scale with low willingness to pay. Free municipal portals and the platforms' own fields cover the job. I did not confirm whether channel managers have a number field. I found no municipality count or host count (BNetzA list not opened). Niche, weak recurrence.

result.market: Not quantified; no register or statistic found
result.reason: The duty is real. The operator must keep records and arrange leak checks under EU Reg 2024/573, and records are kept for at least 5 years. The German ChemKlimaschutzV Neufassung reportedly applies from 17 April 2026 (IHK Braunschweig, secondary source; Bundesgesetzblatt not checked). Competition exists: VDKF-LEC (with an operator version), Mobilec and Clim'app are all aimed at contractors. In practice the Kälte contractor logs the system and schedules checks, so small operators rarely buy software. Many operators are affected, but willingness to pay is low and the buyer is fragmented. I did not verify 2024/573 intervals, the penalty (older sources say up to 50,000 EUR), or any market count. I left the verdict at unverifiable because the 2024/573 intervals, the penalty and the market size are unchecked.
